==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*leǵ-}}
Borrowed from {{bor|en|la|ēlēctus}}, past participle of {{m|la|ēligō||to pick out, choose, elect}}, from {{m|la|ē-||out}} + {{m|la|legō||to pick out, pick, gather, collect, etc.}}; see {{m|en|legend}}.

Cognate to {{m|en|eclectic}}, which is via {{cog|grc|-}} rather than {{cog|la|-}}, hence prefix {{m|grc|ἐκ}}, rather than {{m|la|e-}} (from {{m|la|ex}}).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪˈlɛkt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɪˈlɛkt/|/i-/|/ə-/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-elect.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkt|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|s|*}}

# One chosen or set apart.
# {{lb|en|Christian|theology}} Someone chosen by God for [[salvation]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|Isaiah|42|1|passage=Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine '''elect''', in whom my soul delighteth.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Luke|18|7|passage=Shall not God avenge his won '''elect'''?}}
## {{lb|en|Calvinism}} One foreordained to [[Heaven]].

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[choose]] or make a [[decision]] (to do something).
# {{lb|en|transitive}} (Of a group) to officially select one or more candidates in an [[election]] to hold [[office]].
#* {{quote-av|en|speaker=w:Norm Macdonald|title=w:Norm Macdonald Live|year=2014|season=2|number=9|passage={{w|Barack Obama|President Obama}} in a speech this past week said that we should solve the nation's bee problem. Oh, God, we '''elected''' a guy who sympathizes with bees?}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|-}}

# {{lb|en|postpositive}} Who has been [[elected]] in a specified post, but has not yet entered office.
#: {{ux|en|He is the President '''elect'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Austen Sense and Sensibility|chapter=16|passage=She began almost to feel a dislike of Edward; and it ended, as every feeling must end with her, by carrying back her thoughts to Willoughby, whose manners formed a contrast sufficiently striking to those of his brother '''elect'''.}}
# Chosen; taken by preference from among two or more.
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=III|canto=VII|passage=colours quaint '''elect'''}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|1 Timothy|5|21|passage=the '''elect''' angels}}

====Usage notes====
When denoting someone who has been elected but not yet entered office, the title is usually hyphenated (e.g. {{m|en|president-elect}}, ''senator-elect'', ''representative-elect'', ''mayor-elect'', etc.). The plural forms are created by pluralizing the office (e.g. ''presidents-elect'', ''senators-elect'', ''representatives-elect'', ''mayors-elect'', etc.).
